verdict_first_line: FOR the paper's crossover-profile claim, on the PRE-REGISTERED wave-1 data alone: the low-s_d arm is now LOCATED - at s_d=0.00125 under both estimators (half-drop 1.56 [0.489, 2.38]; legacy 3.04 [1.59, 3.18]) and at s_d=0.0005 under the half-drop estimator (2.88 [0.794, 7.02]; the legacy level-1/2 crossing there sits at the edge of the pre-registered range, 0.947 replicate validity) - but the trough-vertex functional FORM is NOT decided by the pre-registered data (half-drop selects quadratic, legacy selects piecewise); a NON-pre-registered post-hoc extension (wave 2) is disclosed and reported only as a labelled sensitivity variant.

estimator_reconciliation_vs_deposit.note: legacy level-0.5 loglin crossing recomputed on the deposited pool with the pooled 2,856-run neutral anchor reproduces the round-7 deposited theta_star per rung

load_axis_convention: theta = U_d/s_d = mud/sd (U_d = mud, deposited convention)

estimators.half_drop: convention-free: load at which log median T_fix falls halfway between the ladder's low-load plateau (anchor + flat low rungs, 2-SE band) and its high-load plateau (flat top set); first descending crossing, log-linear interpolation in theta; plateaus re-derived in every bootstrap replicate
estimators.level_half: legacy deposit estimator: theta at which median T_fix / neutral-anchor median crosses 1/2 (ridge_analysis.loglin_cross), isotonic variant also reported
estimators.bootstrap: run-level, B=2000, every rung and the anchor resampled; CIs = 2.5/97.5 percentiles; each estimate stored [value, ci_lo, ci_hi]

new_rungs_bounded.0.0005: half-drop located; legacy marginal (0.947 replicate validity, crossing at range edge)

sd_0.00125.status: LOCATED under both estimators on wave-1 data (finite two-sided CIs, bootstrap validity 1.00 for both).
sd_0.00125.prior_round8_status: lower bound only: round-8 ladder sampled theta<=1.6, own-anchor ratio bottomed at 0.554 with no half crossing

sd_0.0005.status: half-drop crossing LOCATED (finite CI, validity 1.00). Legacy level-1/2 has a finite CI but only 0.947 of bootstrap replicates cross 1/2 within the pre-registered range theta<=51.2 (top-rung ratio hovers at 0.47-0.52), i.e. the legacy crossing sits at the edge of the sampled range: located under half-drop, marginal (near the range edge) under the legacy convention.

vertex_model_comparison.criterion: AICc on WLS Gaussian likelihood, weights 1/var_log(theta*) from run-level bootstrap; selection frequency across a joint bootstrap is the model-uncertainty summary
vertex_model_comparison.form_ambiguity_note: On the pre-registered data the two estimators DISAGREE on the vertex form: half-drop selects quadratic_in_log_sd (piecewise dAICc 3.7, selection freq quadratic 0.57 / piecewise 0.41), legacy level-1/2 selects piecewise_linear (freq 0.97). The vertex location is bracketed roughly between ~3.5e-3 (piecewise) and ~7.8e-3 (quadratic) but its functional form is not resolved by these data.

high_plateau_caveat.finding: At s_d=0.0005 and 0.00125 the loaded median T_fix does NOT reach a clean finite high-load asymptote within the pre-registered load range; the top of each ladder is still declining slowly rather than sitting on a flat shelf.
high_plateau_caveat.consequence: Because the ratio only just dips through 1/2 near the top of the pre-registered ranges and the high plateau is only marginally resolved (plateau-resolution bootstrap fractions reported per rung), the half-drop and legacy estimators can differ: they diverge strongly at s_d=0.0005 (half-drop 2.88 vs legacy 25.8, the latter with 0.947 replicate validity, sitting at the range edge) and moderately at 0.00125 (1.56 vs 3.04). The estimator disagreement is reported as an honest measure of the plateau ambiguity; the intervals are finite and two-sided under both conventions except where flagged marginal.

runtime_note: 14,728 runs on one 64-core host (60 workers): pre-registered wave 1 (12,680 runs) in 53.0 min plus the post-hoc wave 2 (2,048 runs) in 6.0 min; ~52 core-hours of kernel time; no rung was run at reduced replication. All PRIMARY estimates use wave 1 only.
primary_dataset: wave1 (12,680 pre-registered runs). Wave 2 (2,048 runs) was launched on a criterion NOT satisfying the pre-registered adaptive-extension rule and is therefore reported ONLY as a labelled post-hoc sensitivity variant; every headline number is computed on wave 1 alone.

preregistration_deviation_disclosure.what_the_rule_said: adaptive_extension_rule high-side trigger: extend a ladder upward ONLY IF its rung-median ratio has not descended through 0.5 by its top rung

what_was_observed_after_wave1.note: both ratios were ALREADY below 0.5 at the top rung, so the pre-registered trigger was FALSE for both ladders

preregistration_deviation_disclosure.what_was_done: wave 2 (2,048 runs, seeds 13,820,000-13,822,047: x2 high-load extensions plus densification) was nonetheless launched, using a different, undeclared criterion (top of ladder 'still descending' / plateau-flatness), i.e. a post-hoc decision the pre-registration was written to foreclose.
preregistration_deviation_disclosure.how_it_is_treated: wave 2 is EXCLUDED from every primary estimate; it is retained in low_sd_runs.parquet with wave='wave2_posthoc' and reported below strictly as a labelled post-hoc sensitivity variant. It must not be described as pre-registered.
preregistration_deviation_disclosure.impact_on_conclusions: the verdict (arm bounded at both new rungs) holds on wave 1 alone; the point estimates and the vertex form-selection DO change materially between wave-1-only and wave-2-inclusive, so the wave-1 numbers are the ones to quote.

posthoc_sensitivity_wave2_included.status: NOT pre-registered; post-hoc extension; sensitivity variant only - do not quote as primary
